panel.title: Tomorrow X, day 2 (Nov 18, Austin): AI credit panel with Andrew West (Oaktree) and Scott Goodwin (Diameter)
points: Market sizes: ~$10T investment grade, ~$1.5T high yield, ~$1.5T private credit/BSL, ~$40T asset-backed financing. The $40T matches Apollo's estimate of the whole private origination market (mortgages, consumer, equipment, trade), not AI-eligible collateral.
Chip financing at 60–80% loan-to-cost adds up to ~$1.5T of debt, which will pressure spreads. Lenders cap concentration (~10% of a fund), so the pools are not fully available to AI.

Borrowing-cost ladder on comparable chip collateral: ~7.5–8% backed by NVIDIA/Broadcom, ~8.5% SpaceX holdco, ~9% CoreWeave bonds, ~12% stronger neoclouds, 15%+ with warrants for small inference providers. Unsecured neocloud debt ~15%, up from ~7% a year ago.
Prepayments and residual-value guarantees are not free. Goodwin likes 2-year chip loans backed by highly rated companies at ~300bp over cash, and some neocloud/powered-shell converts at 50–70 cents.

pools.note: The headline pools are large: ~$9.6T US IG, ~$4.1T global private credit, ~$9.6T of life-insurer assets. The constraint is the slice that can take AI risk. Concentration caps (~3% per issuer at insurers, ~10% per sector at funds) and falling loan-to-cost push more of the build onto equity and hyperscaler cash flow. JPM has debt funding ~59% of 2027–31 AI capex, down from 70–95% loan-to-cost on 2026 deals.
